translations.kjv: And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire.
translations.ylt: `And if thine eye doth cause thee to stumble, pluck it out and cast from thee; it is good for thee one-eyed to enter into the life, rather than having two eyes to be cast to the gehenna of the fire.
translations.web: If your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast it from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna of fire.

translations.kjv: Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.
translations.ylt: `Beware! --ye may not despise one of these little ones, for I say to you, that their messengers in the heavens do always behold the face of my Father who is in the heavens,
translations.web: See that you don’t despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that in heaven their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.

translations.kjv: How think ye? if a man have an hundred sheep, and one of them be gone astray, doth he not leave the ninety and nine, and goeth into the mountains, and seeketh that which is gone astray?
translations.ylt: `What think ye? if a man may have an hundred sheep, and there may go astray one of them, doth he not--having left the ninety-nine, having gone on the mountains--seek that which is gone astray?
translations.web: “What do you think? If a man has one hundred sheep, and one of them goes astray, doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine, go to the mountains, and seek that which has gone astray?

translations.kjv: And if so be that he find it, verily I say unto you, he rejoiceth more of that sheep, than of the ninety and nine which went not astray.
translations.ylt: and if it may come to pass that he doth find it, verily I say to you, that he doth rejoice over it more than over the ninety-nine that have not gone astray;
translations.web: If he finds it, most certainly I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine which have not gone astray.

translations.kjv: Even so it is not the will of your Father which is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish.
translations.ylt: so it is not will in presence of your Father who is in the heavens, that one of these little ones may perish.
translations.web: Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

translations.kjv: Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.
translations.ylt: `And if thy brother may sin against thee, go and show him his fault between thee and him alone, if he may hear thee, thou didst gain thy brother;
translations.web: “If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.

translations.kjv: But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
translations.ylt: and if he may not hear, take with thee yet one or two, that by the mouth of two witnesses or three every word may stand.
translations.web: But if he doesn’t listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.

translations.kjv: And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.
translations.ylt: `And if he may not hear them, say it to the assembly, and if also the assembly he may not hear, let him be to thee as the heathen man and the tax-gatherer.
translations.web: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly. If he refuses to hear the assembly also, let him be to you as a Gentile or a tax collector.

translations.kjv: Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
translations.ylt: `Verily I say to you, Whatever things ye may bind upon the earth shall be having been bound in the heavens, and whatever things ye may loose on the earth shall be having been loosed in the heavens.
translations.web: Most certainly I tell you, whatever things you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever things you release on earth will have been released in heaven.

translations.kjv: Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.
translations.ylt: `Again, I say to you, that, if two of you may agree on the earth concerning anything, whatever they may ask--it shall be done to them from my Father who is in the heavens,
translations.web: Again, assuredly I tell you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.

translations.kjv: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
translations.ylt: for where there are two or three gathered together--to my name, there am I in the midst of them.'
translations.web: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”

translations.kjv: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?
translations.ylt: Then Peter having come near to him, said, `Sir, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him--till seven times?'
translations.web: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?”

translations.kjv: Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.
translations.ylt: Jesus saith to him, `I do not say to thee till seven times, but till seventy times seven.
translations.web: Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.

translations.kjv: Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, which would take account of his servants.
translations.ylt: `Because of this was the reign of the heavens likened to a man, a king, who did will to take reckoning with his servants,
translations.web: Therefore the Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.

translations.kjv: And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought unto him, which owed him ten thousand talents.
translations.ylt: and he having begun to take account, there was brought near to him one debtor of a myriad of talents,
translations.web: When he had begun to settle, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents.

translations.kjv: But forasmuch as he had not to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.
translations.ylt: and he having nothing to pay, his lord did command him to be sold, and his wife, and the children, and all, whatever he had, and payment to be made.
translations.web: But because he couldn’t pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, with his wife, his children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.

translations.kjv: The servant therefore fell down, and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.
translations.ylt: The servant then, having fallen down, was bowing to him, saying, Sir, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all;
translations.web: The servant therefore fell down and knelt before him, saying, ‘Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay you all!’

translations.kjv: Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt.
translations.ylt: and the lord of that servant having been moved with compassion did release him, and the debt he forgave him.
translations.web: The lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him and forgave him the debt.

translations.kjv: But the same servant went out, and found one of his fellowservants, which owed him an hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that thou owest.
translations.ylt: `And, that servant having come forth, found one of his fellow-servants who was owing him an hundred denaries, and having laid hold, he took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that which thou owest.
translations.web: “But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him one hundred denarii, and he grabbed him and took him by the throat, saying, ‘Pay me what you owe!’

translations.kjv: And his fellowservant fell down at his feet, and besought him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.
translations.ylt: His fellow-servant then, having fallen down at his feet, was calling on him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay thee all;
translations.web: “So his fellow servant fell down at his feet and begged him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you!’

translations.kjv: And he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay the debt.
translations.ylt: and he would not, but having gone away, he cast him into prison, till he might pay that which was owing.
translations.web: He would not, but went and cast him into prison until he should pay back that which was due.

translations.kjv: So when his fellowservants saw what was done, they were very sorry, and came and told unto their lord all that was done.
translations.ylt: `And his fellow-servants having seen the things that were done, were grieved exceedingly, and having come, shewed fully to their lord all the things that were done;
translations.web: So when his fellow servants saw what was done, they were exceedingly sorry, and came and told their lord all that was done.

translations.kjv: Then his lord, after that he had called him, said unto him, O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me:
translations.ylt: then having called him, his lord saith to him, Evil servant! all that debt I did forgive thee, seeing thou didst call upon me,
translations.web: Then his lord called him in and said to him, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you begged me.

translations.kjv: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee?
translations.ylt: did it not behove also thee to have dealt kindly with thy fellow-servant, as I also dealt kindly with thee?
translations.web: Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?’

translations.kjv: And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors, till he should pay all that was due unto him.
translations.ylt: `And having been wroth, his lord delivered him to the inquisitors, till he might pay all that was owing to him;
translations.web: His lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors until he should pay all that was due to him.

translations.kjv: So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.
translations.ylt: so also my heavenly Father will do to you, if ye may not forgive each one his brother from your hearts their trespasses.'
translations.web: So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don’t each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.”

translations.kjv: And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these sayings, he departed from Galilee, and came into the coasts of Judea beyond Jordan;
translations.ylt: And it came to pass, when Jesus finished these words, he removed from Galilee, and did come to the borders of Judea, beyond the Jordan,
translations.web: When Jesus had finished these words, he departed from Galilee and came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.

translations.kjv: And great multitudes followed him; and he healed them there.
translations.ylt: and great multitudes followed him, and he healed them there.
translations.web: Great multitudes followed him, and he healed them there.

translations.kjv: The Pharisees also came unto him, tempting him, and saying unto him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?
translations.ylt: And the Pharisees came near to him, tempting him, and saying to him, `Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?'
translations.web: Pharisees came to him, testing him and saying, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”

translations.kjv: And he answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female,
translations.ylt: And he answering said to them, `Did ye not read, that He who made them, from the beginning a male and a female made them,
translations.web: He answered, “Haven’t you read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female,

translations.kjv: And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?
translations.ylt: and said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and cleave to his wife, and they shall be--the two--for one flesh?
translations.web: and said, ‘For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh’?

translations.kjv: Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
translations.ylt: so that they are no more two, but one flesh; what therefore God did join together, let no man put asunder.'
translations.web: So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.”

translations.kjv: They say unto him, Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away?
translations.ylt: They say to him, `Why then did Moses command to give a roll of divorce, and to put her away?'
translations.web: They asked him, “Why then did Moses command us to give her a certificate of divorce and divorce her?”

translations.kjv: He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so.
translations.ylt: He saith to them--`Moses for your stiffness of heart did suffer you to put away your wives, but from the beginning it hath not been so.
translations.web: He said to them, “Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.

translations.kjv: And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.
translations.ylt: `And I say to you, that, whoever may put away his wife, if not for whoredom, and may marry another, doth commit adultery; and he who did marry her that hath been put away, doth commit adultery.'
translations.web: I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery; and he who marries her when she is divorced commits adultery.”

translations.kjv: His disciples say unto him, If the case of the man be so with his wife, it is not good to marry.
translations.ylt: His disciples say to him, `If the case of the man with the woman is so, it is not good to marry.'
translations.web: His disciples said to him, “If this is the case of the man with his wife, it is not expedient to marry.”

translations.kjv: But he said unto them, All men cannot receive this saying, save they to whom it is given.
translations.ylt: And he said to them, `All do not receive this word, but those to whom it hath been given;
translations.web: But he said to them, “Not all men can receive this saying, but those to whom it is given.

translations.kjv: For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother’s womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men: and there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven’s sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it.
translations.ylt: for there are eunuchs who from the mother's womb were so born; and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who kept themselves eunuchs because of the reign of the heavens: he who is able to receive it --let him receive.'
translations.web: For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the Kingdom of Heaven’s sake. He who is able to receive it, let him receive it.”

translations.kjv: Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them.
translations.ylt: Then were brought near to him children that he might put hands on them and pray, and the disciples rebuked them.
translations.web: Then little children were brought to him that he should lay his hands on them and pray; and the disciples rebuked them.

translations.kjv: But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
translations.ylt: But Jesus said, `Suffer the children, and forbid them not, to come unto me, for of such is the reign of the heavens;'
translations.web: But Jesus said, “Allow the little children, and don’t forbid them to come to me; for the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to ones like these.”

translations.kjv: And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence.
translations.ylt: and having laid on them his hands, he departed thence.
translations.web: He laid his hands on them, and departed from there.

translations.kjv: And, behold, one came and said unto him, Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?
translations.ylt: And lo, one having come near, said to him, `Good teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have life age-during?'
translations.web: Behold, one came to him and said, “Good teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?”

translations.kjv: And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God: but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.
translations.ylt: And he said to him, `Why me dost thou call good? no one is good except One--God; but if thou dost will to enter into the life, keep the commands.'
translations.web: He said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good but one, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”

translations.kjv: He saith unto him, Which? Jesus said, Thou shalt do no murder, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness,
translations.ylt: He saith to him, `What kind?' And Jesus said, `Thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not bear false witness,
translations.web: He said to him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder.’ ‘You shall not commit adultery.’ ‘You shall not steal.’ ‘You shall not offer false testimony.’

translations.kjv: Honour thy father and thy mother: and, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
translations.ylt: honour thy father and mother, and, thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.'
translations.web: ‘Honor your father and your mother.’ And, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”

translations.kjv: The young man saith unto him, All these things have I kept from my youth up: what lack I yet?
translations.ylt: The young man saith to him, `All these did I keep from my youth; what yet do I lack?'
translations.web: The young man said to him, “All these things I have observed from my youth. What do I still lack?”

translations.kjv: Jesus said unto him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.
translations.ylt: Jesus said to him, `If thou dost will to be perfect, go away, sell what thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven, and come, follow me.'
translations.web: Jesus said to him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”

translations.kjv: But when the young man heard that saying, he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions.
translations.ylt: And the young man, having heard the word, went away sorrowful, for he had many possessions;
translations.web: But when the young man heard this, he went away sad, for he was one who had great possessions.

translations.kjv: Then said Jesus unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven.
translations.ylt: and Jesus said to his disciples, `Verily I say to you, that hardly shall a rich man enter into the reign of the heavens;
translations.web: Jesus said to his disciples, “Most certainly I say to you, a rich man will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven with difficulty.

translations.kjv: And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
translations.ylt: and again I say to you, it is easier for a camel through the eye of a needle to go, than for a rich man to enter into the reign of God.'
translations.web: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”

translations.kjv: When his disciples heard it, they were exceedingly amazed, saying, Who then can be saved?
translations.ylt: And his disciples having heard, were amazed exceedingly, saying, `Who, then, is able to be saved?'
translations.web: When the disciples heard it, they were exceedingly astonished, saying, “Who then can be saved?”

translations.kjv: But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
translations.ylt: And Jesus having earnestly beheld, said to them, `With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.'
translations.web: Looking at them, Jesus said, “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”

translations.kjv: Then answered Peter and said unto him, Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee; what shall we have therefore?
translations.ylt: Then Peter answering said to him, `Lo, we did leave all, and follow thee, what then shall we have?'
translations.web: Then Peter answered, “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. What then will we have?”

translations.kjv: And Jesus said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
translations.ylt: And Jesus said to them, `Verily I say to you, that ye who did follow me, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man may sit upon a throne of his glory, shall sit--ye also--upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel;
translations.web: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly I tell you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Man will sit on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

translations.kjv: And every one that hath forsaken houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, shall receive an hundredfold, and shall inherit everlasting life.
translations.ylt: and every one who left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields, for my name's sake, an hundredfold shall receive, and life age-during shall inherit;
translations.web: Everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, will receive one hundred times, and will inherit eternal life.

translations.kjv: But many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first.
translations.ylt: and many first shall be last, and last first.
translations.web: But many will be last who are first, and first who are last.

translations.kjv: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.
translations.ylt: `For the reign of the heavens is like to a man, a householder, who went forth with the morning to hire workmen for his vineyard,
translations.web: “For the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who was the master of a household, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard.

translations.kjv: And when he had agreed with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
translations.ylt: and having agreed with the workmen for a denary a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
translations.web: When he had agreed with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

translations.kjv: And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace,
translations.ylt: `And having gone forth about the third hour, he saw others standing in the market-place idle,
translations.web: He went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace.

translations.kjv: And said unto them; Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you. And they went their way.
translations.ylt: and to these he said, Go ye--also ye--to the vineyard, and whatever may be righteous I will give you;
translations.web: He said to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is right I will give you.’ So they went their way.

translations.kjv: Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour, and did likewise.
translations.ylt: and they went away. `Again, having gone forth about the sixth and the ninth hour, he did in like manner.
translations.web: Again he went out about the sixth and the ninth hour, and did likewise.

translations.kjv: And about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing idle, and saith unto them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?
translations.ylt: And about the eleventh hour, having gone forth, he found others standing idle, and saith to them, Why here have ye stood all the day idle?
translations.web: About the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing idle. He said to them, ‘Why do you stand here all day idle?’

translations.kjv: They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith unto them, Go ye also into the vineyard; and whatsoever is right, that shall ye receive.
translations.ylt: they say to him, Because no one did hire us; he saith to them, Go ye--ye also--to the vineyard, and whatever may be righteous ye shall receive.
translations.web: “They said to him, ‘Because no one has hired us.’ “He said to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and you will receive whatever is right.’

translations.kjv: So when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.
translations.ylt: `And evening having come, the lord of the vineyard saith to his steward, Call the workmen, and pay them the reward, having begun from the last--unto the first.
translations.web: “When evening had come, the lord of the vineyard said to his manager, ‘Call the laborers and pay them their wages, beginning from the last to the first.’

translations.kjv: And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny.
translations.ylt: And they of about the eleventh hour having come, did receive each a denary.
translations.web: “When those who were hired at about the eleventh hour came, they each received a denarius.

translations.kjv: But when the first came, they supposed that they should have received more; and they likewise received every man a penny.
translations.ylt: `And the first having come, did suppose that they shall receive more, and they received, they also, each a denary,
translations.web: When the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; and they likewise each received a denarius.

translations.kjv: And when they had received it, they murmured against the goodman of the house,
translations.ylt: and having received it, they were murmuring against the householder, saying,
translations.web: When they received it, they murmured against the master of the household,

translations.kjv: Saying, These last have wrought but one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day.
translations.ylt: that These, the last, wrought one hour, and thou didst make them equal to us, who were bearing the burden of the day--and the heat.
translations.web: saying, ‘These last have spent one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat!’

translations.kjv: But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a penny?
translations.ylt: `And he answering said to one of them, Comrade, I do no unrighteousness to thee; for a denary didst not thou agree with me?
translations.web: “But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Didn’t you agree with me for a denarius?

translations.kjv: Take that thine is, and go thy way: I will give unto this last, even as unto thee.
translations.ylt: take that which is thine, and go; and I will to give to this, the last, also as to thee;
translations.web: Take that which is yours, and go your way. It is my desire to give to this last just as much as to you.

translations.kjv: Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? Is thine eye evil, because I am good?
translations.ylt: is it not lawful to me to do what I will in mine own? is thine eye evil because I am good?
translations.web: Isn’t it lawful for me to do what I want to with what I own? Or is your eye evil, because I am good?’

translations.kjv: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.
translations.ylt: So the last shall be first, and the first last, for many are called, and few chosen.'
translations.web: So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.”

translations.kjv: And Jesus going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them,
translations.ylt: And Jesus going up to Jerusalem, took the twelve disciples by themselves in the way, and said to them,
translations.web: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside, and on the way he said to them,

translations.kjv: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be betrayed unto the chief priests and unto the scribes, and they shall condemn him to death,
translations.ylt: `Lo, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man shall be delivered to the chief priests and scribes,
translations.web: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death,

translations.kjv: And shall deliver him to the Gentiles to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify him: and the third day he shall rise again.
translations.ylt: and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him to the nations to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify, and the third day he will rise again.'
translations.web: and will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock, to scourge, and to crucify; and the third day he will be raised up.”

translations.kjv: Then came to him the mother of Zebedee’s children with her sons, worshipping him, and desiring a certain thing of him.
translations.ylt: Then came near to him the mother of the sons of Zebedee, with her sons, bowing and asking something from him,
translations.web: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, kneeling and asking a certain thing of him.

translations.kjv: And he said unto her, What wilt thou? She saith unto him, Grant that these my two sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other on the left, in thy kingdom.
translations.ylt: and he said to her, `What wilt thou?' She saith to him, `Say, that they may sit--these my two sons--one on thy right hand, and one on the left, in thy reign.'
translations.web: He said to her, “What do you want?” She said to him, “Command that these, my two sons, may sit, one on your right hand and one on your left hand, in your Kingdom.”

translations.kjv: But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.
translations.ylt: And Jesus answering said, `Ye have not known what ye ask for yourselves; are ye able to drink of the cup that I am about to drink? and with the baptism that I am baptized with, to be baptized?' They say to him, `We are able.'
translations.web: But Jesus answered, “You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?” They said to him, “We are able.”

translations.kjv: And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.
translations.ylt: And he saith to them, `Of my cup indeed ye shall drink, and with the baptism that I am baptized with ye shall be baptized; but to sit on my right hand and on my left is not mine to give, but--to those for whom it hath been prepared by my father.'
translations.web: He said to them, “You will indeed drink my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with; but to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give, but it is for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”

translations.kjv: And when the ten heard it, they were moved with indignation against the two brethren.
translations.ylt: And the ten having heard, were much displeased with the two brothers,
translations.web: When the ten heard it, they were indignant with the two brothers.

translations.kjv: But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them.
translations.ylt: and Jesus having called them near, said, `Ye have known that the rulers of the nations do exercise lordship over them, and those great do exercise authority over them,
translations.web: But Jesus summoned them, and said, “You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.

translations.kjv: But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;
translations.ylt: but not so shall it be among you, but whoever may will among you to become great, let him be your ministrant;
translations.web: It shall not be so among you; but whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant.

translations.kjv: And whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant:
translations.ylt: and whoever may will among you to be first, let him be your servant;
translations.web: Whoever desires to be first among you shall be your bondservant,

translations.kjv: Even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
translations.ylt: even as the Son of Man did not come to be ministered to, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.'
translations.web: even as the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

translations.kjv: And as they departed from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.
translations.ylt: And they going forth from Jericho, there followed him a great multitude,
translations.web: As they went out from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.

translations.kjv: And, behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Jesus passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, thou Son of David.
translations.ylt: and lo, two blind men sitting by the way, having heard that Jesus doth pass by, cried, saying, `Deal kindly with us, sir--Son of David.'
translations.web: Behold, two blind men sitting by the road, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, “Lord, have mercy on us, you son of David!”

translations.kjv: And the multitude rebuked them, because they should hold their peace: but they cried the more, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, thou Son of David.
translations.ylt: And the multitude charged them that they might be silent, and they cried out the more, saying, `Deal kindly with us sir--Son of David.'
translations.web: The multitude rebuked them, telling them that they should be quiet, but they cried out even more, “Lord, have mercy on us, you son of David!”

translations.kjv: And Jesus stood still, and called them, and said, What will ye that I shall do unto you?
translations.ylt: And having stood, Jesus called them, and said, `What will ye that I may do to you?'
translations.web: Jesus stood still and called them, and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”

translations.kjv: They say unto him, Lord, that our eyes may be opened.
translations.ylt: they say to him, `Sir, that our eyes may be opened;'
translations.web: They told him, “Lord, that our eyes may be opened.”

translations.kjv: So Jesus had compassion on them, and touched their eyes: and immediately their eyes received sight, and they followed him.
translations.ylt: and having been moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and immediately their eyes received sight, and they followed him.
translations.web: Jesus, being moved with compassion, touched their eyes; and immediately their eyes received their sight, and they followed him.

translations.kjv: And when they drew nigh unto Jerusalem, and were come to Bethphage, unto the mount of Olives, then sent Jesus two disciples,
translations.ylt: And when they came nigh to Jerusalem, and came to Bethphage, unto the mount of the Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
translations.web: When they came near to Jerusalem and came to Bethsphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,

translations.kjv: Saying unto them, Go into the village over against you, and straightway ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them, and bring them unto me.
translations.ylt: saying to them, `Go on to the village over-against you, and immediately ye shall find an ass bound, and a colt with her--having loosed, bring ye to me;
translations.web: saying to them, “Go into the village that is opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them to me.

translations.kjv: And if any man say ought unto you, ye shall say, The Lord hath need of them; and straightway he will send them.
translations.ylt: and if any one may say anything to you, ye shall say, that the lord hath need of them, and immediately he will send them.'
translations.web: If anyone says anything to you, you shall say, ‘The Lord needs them,’ and immediately he will send them.”

translations.kjv: All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying,
translations.ylt: And all this came to pass, that it might be fulfilled that was spoken through the prophet, saying,
translations.web: All this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,

translations.kjv: Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.
translations.ylt: `Tell ye the daughter of Zion, Lo, thy king doth come to thee, meek, and mounted on an ass, and a colt, a foal of a beast of burden.'
translations.web: “Tell the daughter of Zion, behold, your King comes to you, humble, and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.”

translations.kjv: And the disciples went, and did as Jesus commanded them,
translations.ylt: And the disciples having gone and having done as Jesus commanded them,
translations.web: The disciples went and did just as Jesus commanded them,

translations.kjv: And brought the ass, and the colt, and put on them their clothes, and they set him thereon.
translations.ylt: brought the ass and the colt, and did put on them their garments, and set him upon them;
translations.web: and brought the donkey and the colt and laid their clothes on them; and he sat on them.

translations.kjv: And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and strawed them in the way.
translations.ylt: and the very great multitude spread their own garments in the way, and others were cutting branches from the trees, and were strewing in the way,
translations.web: A very great multitude spread their clothes on the road. Others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.

translations.kjv: And the multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.
translations.ylt: and the multitudes who were going before, and who were following, were crying, saying, `Hosanna to the Son of David, blessed is he who is coming in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.'
translations.web: The multitudes who went in front of him, and those who followed, kept shouting, “Hosanna to the son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”

translations.kjv: And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this?
translations.ylt: And he having entered into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, `Who is this?'
translations.web: When he had come into Jerusalem, all the city was stirred up, saying, “Who is this?”

translations.kjv: And the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee.
translations.ylt: And the multitudes said, `This is Jesus the prophet, who is from Nazareth of Galilee.'
translations.web: The multitudes said, “This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.”

translations.kjv: And Jesus went into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,
translations.ylt: And Jesus entered into the temple of God, and did cast forth all those selling and buying in the temple, and the tables of the money-changers he overturned, and the seats of those selling the doves,
translations.web: Jesus entered into the temple of God and drove out all of those who sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.

translations.kjv: And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.
translations.ylt: and he saith to them, `It hath been written, My house a house of prayer shall be called, but ye did make it a den of robbers.'
translations.web: He said to them, “It is written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a den of robbers!”

translations.kjv: And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple; and he healed them.
translations.ylt: And there came to him blind and lame men in the temple, and he healed them,
translations.web: The lame and the blind came to him in the temple, and he healed them.

translations.kjv: And when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the Son of David; they were sore displeased,
translations.ylt: and the chief priests and the scribes having seen the wonderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, `Hosanna to the Son of David,' were much displeased;
translations.web: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children who were crying in the temple and saying, “Hosanna to the son of David!” they were indignant,

translations.kjv: And said unto him, Hearest thou what these say? And Jesus saith unto them, Yea; have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?
translations.ylt: and they said to him, `Hearest thou what these say?' And Jesus saith to them, `Yes, did ye never read, that, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings Thou didst prepare praise?'
translations.web: and said to him, “Do you hear what these are saying?” Jesus said to them, “Yes. Did you never read, ‘Out of the mouth of children and nursing babies, you have perfected praise’?”

translations.kjv: And he left them, and went out of the city into Bethany; and he lodged there.
translations.ylt: And having left them, he went forth out of the city to Bethany, and did lodge there,
translations.web: He left them and went out of the city to Bethany, and camped there.

translations.kjv: Now in the morning as he returned into the city, he hungered.
translations.ylt: and in the morning turning back to the city, he hungered,
translations.web: Now in the morning, as he returned to the city, he was hungry.

translations.kjv: And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.
translations.ylt: and having seen a certain fig-tree on the way, he came to it, and found nothing in it except leaves only, and he saith to it, `No more from thee may fruit be--to the age;' and forthwith the fig-tree withered.
translations.web: Seeing a fig tree by the road, he came to it and found nothing on it but leaves. He said to it, “Let there be no fruit from you forever!” Immediately the fig tree withered away.

translations.kjv: And when the disciples saw it, they marvelled, saying, How soon is the fig tree withered away!
translations.ylt: And the disciples having seen, did wonder, saying, `How did the fig-tree forthwith wither?'
translations.web: When the disciples saw it, they marveled, saying, “How did the fig tree immediately wither away?”

translations.kjv: Jesus answered and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do this which is done to the fig tree, but also if ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; it shall be done.
translations.ylt: And Jesus answering said to them, `Verily I say to you, If ye may have faith, and may not doubt, not only this of the fig-tree shall ye do, but even if to this mount ye may say, Be lifted up and be cast into the sea, it shall come to pass;
translations.web: Jesus answered them, “Most certainly I tell you, if you have faith and don’t doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you told this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ it would be done.

translations.kjv: And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.
translations.ylt: and all--as much as ye may ask in the prayer, believing, ye shall receive.'
translations.web: All things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive.”

translations.kjv: And when he was come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came unto him as he was teaching, and said, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority?
translations.ylt: And he having come to the temple, there came to him when teaching the chief priests and the elders of the people, saying, `By what authority dost thou do these things? and who gave thee this authority?'
translations.web: When he had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching, and said, “By what authority do you do these things? Who gave you this authority?”

translations.kjv: And Jesus answered and said unto them, I also will ask you one thing, which if ye tell me, I in like wise will tell you by what authority I do these things.
translations.ylt: And Jesus answering said to them, `I will ask you--I also--one word, which if ye may tell me, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things;
translations.web: Jesus answered them, “I also will ask you one question, which if you tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.

translations.kjv: The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven, or of men? And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say unto us, Why did ye not then believe him?
translations.ylt: the baptism of John, whence was it? --from heaven, or from men?' And they were reasoning with themselves, saying, `If we should say, From heaven; he will say to us, Wherefore, then, did ye not believe him?
translations.web: The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven or from men?” They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will ask us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

translations.kjv: But if we shall say, Of men; we fear the people; for all hold John as a prophet.
translations.ylt: and if we should say, From men, we fear the multitude, for all hold John as a prophet.'
translations.web: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we fear the multitude, for all hold John as a prophet.”

translations.kjv: And they answered Jesus, and said, We cannot tell. And he said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.
translations.ylt: And answering Jesus they said, `We have not known.' He said to them--he also--`Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
translations.web: They answered Jesus, and said, “We don’t know.” He also said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.

translations.kjv: But what think ye? A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to day in my vineyard.
translations.ylt: `And what think ye? A man had two children, and having come to the first, he said, Child, go, to-day be working in my vineyard.'
translations.web: But what do you think? A man had two sons, and he came to the first, and said, ‘Son, go work today in my vineyard.’

translations.kjv: He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went.
translations.ylt: And he answering said, `I will not,' but at last, having repented, he went.
translations.web: He answered, ‘I will not,’ but afterward he changed his mind, and went.

translations.kjv: And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.
translations.ylt: `And having come to the second, he said in the same manner, and he answering said, I go, sir, and went not;
translations.web: He came to the second, and said the same thing. He answered, ‘I’m going, sir,’ but he didn’t go.

translations.kjv: Whether of them twain did the will of his father? They say unto him, The first. Jesus saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.
translations.ylt: which of the two did the will of the father?' They say to him, `The first.' Jesus saith to them, `Verily I say to you, that the tax-gatherers and the harlots do go before you into the reign of God,
translations.web: Which of the two did the will of his father?” They said to him, “The first.” Jesus said to them, “Most certainly I tell you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering into God’s Kingdom before you.

translations.kjv: For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.
translations.ylt: for John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye did not believe him, and the tax-gatherers and the harlots did believe him, and ye, having seen, repented not at last--to believe him.
translations.web: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you didn’t believe him; but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. When you saw it, you didn’t even repent afterward, that you might believe him.

translations.kjv: Hear another parable: There was a certain householder, which planted a vineyard, and hedged it round about, and digged a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country:
translations.ylt: `Hear ye another simile: There was a certain man, a householder, who planted a vineyard, and did put a hedge round it, and digged in it a wine-press, and built a tower, and gave it out to husbandmen, and went abroad.
translations.web: “Hear another parable. There was a man who was a master of a household who planted a vineyard, set a hedge about it, dug a wine press in it, built a tower, leased it out to farmers, and went into another country.

translations.kjv: And when the time of the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, that they might receive the fruits of it.
translations.ylt: `And when the season of the fruits came nigh, he sent his servants unto the husbandmen, to receive the fruits of it,
translations.web: When the season for the fruit came near, he sent his servants to the farmers to receive his fruit.

translations.kjv: And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.
translations.ylt: and the husbandmen having taken his servants, one they scourged, and one they killed, and one they stoned.
translations.web: The farmers took his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.

translations.kjv: Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they did unto them likewise.
translations.ylt: `Again he sent other servants more than the first, and they did to them in the same manner.
translations.web: Again, he sent other servants more than the first; and they treated them the same way.

translations.kjv: But last of all he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son.
translations.ylt: `And at last he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son;
translations.web: But afterward he sent to them his son, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

translations.kjv: But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance.
translations.ylt: and the husbandmen having seen the son, said among themselves, This is the heir, come, we may kill him, and may possess his inheritance;
translations.web: But the farmers, when they saw the son, said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him and seize his inheritance.’

translations.kjv: And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.
translations.ylt: and having taken him, they cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him;
translations.web: So they took him and threw him out of the vineyard, then killed him.

translations.kjv: When the lord therefore of the vineyard cometh, what will he do unto those husbandmen?
translations.ylt: whenever therefore the lord of the vineyard may come, what will he do to these husbandmen?'
translations.web: When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?”

translations.kjv: They say unto him, He will miserably destroy those wicked men, and will let out his vineyard unto other husbandmen, which shall render him the fruits in their seasons.
translations.ylt: They say to him, `Evil men--he will evilly destroy them, and the vineyard will give out to other husbandmen, who will give back to him the fruits in their seasons.'
translations.web: They told him, “He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will lease out the vineyard to other farmers who will give him the fruit in its season.”

translations.kjv: Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?
translations.ylt: Jesus saith to them, `Did ye never read in the Writings, A stone that the builders disallowed, it became head of a corner; from the Lord hath this come to pass, and it is wonderful in our eyes.
translations.web: Jesus said to them, “Did you never read in the Scriptures, ‘The stone which the builders rejected was made the head of the corner. This was from the Lord. It is marvelous in our eyes’?

translations.kjv: Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.
translations.ylt: `Because of this I say to you, that the reign of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth its fruit;
translations.web: “Therefore I tell you, God’s Kingdom will be taken away from you and will be given to a nation producing its fruit.

translations.kjv: And whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.
translations.ylt: and he who is falling on this stone shall be broken, and on whomsoever it may fall it will crush him to pieces.'
translations.web: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but on whomever it will fall, it will scatter him as dust.”

translations.kjv: And when the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they perceived that he spake of them.
translations.ylt: And the chief priests and the Pharisees having heard his similes, knew that of them he speaketh,
translations.web: When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they perceived that he spoke about them.

translations.kjv: But when they sought to lay hands on him, they feared the multitude, because they took him for a prophet.
translations.ylt: and seeking to lay hold on him, they feared the multitudes, seeing they were holding him as a prophet.
translations.web: When they sought to seize him, they feared the multitudes, because they considered him to be a prophet.

translations.kjv: And Jesus answered and spake unto them again by parables, and said,
translations.ylt: And Jesus answering, again spake to them in similes, saying,
translations.web: Jesus answered and spoke to them again in parables, saying,

translations.kjv: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son,
translations.ylt: `The reign of the heavens was likened to a man, a king, who made marriage-feasts for his son,
translations.web: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king, who made a wedding feast for his son,

translations.kjv: And sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the wedding: and they would not come.
translations.ylt: and he sent forth his servants to call those having been called to the marriage-feasts, and they were not willing to come.
translations.web: and sent out his servants to call those who were invited to the wedding feast, but they would not come.

translations.kjv: Again, he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them which are bidden, Behold, I have prepared my dinner: my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come unto the marriage.
translations.ylt: `Again he sent forth other servants, saying, Say to those who have been called: Lo, my dinner I prepared, my oxen and the fatlings have been killed, and all things are ready, come ye to the marriage-feasts;
translations.web: Again he sent out other servants, saying, ‘Tell those who are invited, “Behold, I have prepared my dinner. My cattle and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready. Come to the wedding feast!”’

translations.kjv: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise:
translations.ylt: and they, having disregarded it, went away, the one to his own field, and the other to his merchandise;
translations.web: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise;

translations.kjv: And the remnant took his servants, and entreated them spitefully, and slew them.
translations.ylt: and the rest, having laid hold on his servants, did insult and slay them.
translations.web: and the rest grabbed his servants, treated them shamefully, and killed them.

translations.kjv: But when the king heard thereof, he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city.
translations.ylt: `And the king having heard, was wroth, and having sent forth his soldiers, he destroyed those murderers, and their city he set on fire;
translations.web: When the king heard that, he was angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.

translations.kjv: Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they which were bidden were not worthy.
translations.ylt: then saith he to his servants, The marriage-feast indeed is ready, and those called were not worthy,
translations.web: “Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding is ready, but those who were invited weren’t worthy.

translations.kjv: Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.
translations.ylt: be going, then, on to the cross-ways, and as many as ye may find, call ye to the marriage-feasts.
translations.web: Go therefore to the intersections of the highways, and as many as you may find, invite to the wedding feast.’

translations.kjv: So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.
translations.ylt: `And those servants, having gone forth to the ways, did gather all, as many as they found, both bad and good, and the marriage-feast apartment was filled with those reclining.
translations.web: Those servants went out into the highways and gathered together as many as they found, both bad and good. The wedding was filled with guests.

translations.kjv: And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment:
translations.ylt: `And the king having come in to view those reclining, saw there a man not clothed with clothing of the marriage-feast,
translations.web: “But when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who didn’t have on wedding clothing,

translations.kjv: And he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless.
translations.ylt: and he saith to him, Comrade, how didst thou come in hither, not having clothing of the marriage-feast? and he was speechless.
translations.web: and he said to him, ‘Friend, how did you come in here not wearing wedding clothing?’ He was speechless.

translations.kjv: Then said the king to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
translations.ylt: `Then said the king to the ministrants, Having bound his feet and hands, take him up and cast forth to the outer darkness, there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth;
translations.web: Then the king said to the servants, ‘Bind him hand and foot, take him away, and throw him into the outer darkness. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.’

translations.kjv: For many are called, but few are chosen.
translations.ylt: for many are called, and few chosen.'
translations.web: For many are called, but few chosen.”

translations.kjv: Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might entangle him in his talk.
translations.ylt: Then the Pharisees having gone, took counsel how they might ensnare him in words,
translations.web: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might entrap him in his talk.

translations.kjv: And they sent out unto him their disciples with the Herodians, saying, Master, we know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth, neither carest thou for any man: for thou regardest not the person of men.
translations.ylt: and they send to him their disciples with the Herodians, saying, `Teacher, we have known that thou art true, and the way of God in truth thou dost teach, and thou art not caring for any one, for thou dost not look to the face of men;
translations.web: They sent their disciples to him, along with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and teach the way of God in truth, no matter whom you teach; for you aren’t partial to anyone.

translations.kjv: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cesar, or not?
translations.ylt: tell us, therefore, what dost thou think? is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar or not?'
translations.web: Tell us therefore, what do you think? Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”

translations.kjv: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?
translations.ylt: And Jesus having known their wickedness, said, `Why me do ye tempt, hypocrites?
translations.web: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, “Why do you test me, you hypocrites?

translations.kjv: Shew me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a penny.
translations.ylt: show me the tribute-coin?' and they brought to him a denary;
translations.web: Show me the tax money.” They brought to him a denarius.

translations.kjv: And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?
translations.ylt: and he saith to them, `Whose is this image and the inscription?'
translations.web: He asked them, “Whose is this image and inscription?”

translations.kjv: They say unto him, Cesar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cesar the things which are Cesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.
translations.ylt: they say to him, `Caesar's;' then saith he to them, `Render therefore the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God;'
translations.web: They said to him, “Caesar’s.” Then he said to them, “Give therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”

translations.kjv: When they had heard these words, they marvelled, and left him, and went their way.
translations.ylt: and having heard they wondered, and having left him they went away.
translations.web: When they heard it, they marveled, and left him and went away.

translations.kjv: The same day came to him the Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection, and asked him,
translations.ylt: In that day there came near to him Sadducees, who are saying there is not a rising again, and they questioned him, saying,
translations.web: On that day Sadducees (those who say that there is no resurrection) came to him. They asked him,

translations.kjv: Saying, Master, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
translations.ylt: `Teacher, Moses said, If any one may die not having children, his brother shall marry his wife, and shall raise up seed to his brother.
translations.web: saying, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If a man dies, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’

translations.kjv: Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first, when he had married a wife, deceased, and, having no issue, left his wife unto his brother:
translations.ylt: `And there were with us seven brothers, and the first having married did die, and not having seed, he left his wife to his brother;
translations.web: Now there were with us seven brothers. The first married and died, and having no offspring left his wife to his brother.

translations.kjv: Likewise the second also, and the third, unto the seventh.
translations.ylt: in like manner also the second, and the third, unto the seventh,
translations.web: In the same way, the second also, and the third, to the seventh.

translations.kjv: And last of all the woman died also.
translations.ylt: and last of all died also the woman;
translations.web: After them all, the woman died.

translations.kjv: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.
translations.ylt: therefore in the rising again, of which of the seven shall she be wife--for all had her?'
translations.web: In the resurrection therefore, whose wife will she be of the seven? For they all had her.”

translations.kjv: Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.
translations.ylt: And Jesus answering said to them, `Ye go astray, not knowing the Writings, nor the power of God;
translations.web: But Jesus answered them, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God.

translations.kjv: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.
translations.ylt: for in the rising again they do not marry, nor are they given in marriage, but are as messengers of God in heaven.
translations.web: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like God’s angels in heaven.

translations.kjv: But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying,
translations.ylt: `And concerning the rising again of the dead, did ye not read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,
translations.web: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,

translations.kjv: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.
translations.ylt: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not a God of dead men, but of living.'
translations.web: ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”

translations.kjv: And when the multitude heard this, they were astonished at his doctrine.
translations.ylt: And having heard, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching;
translations.web: When the multitudes heard it, they were astonished at his teaching.

translations.kjv: But when the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, they were gathered together.
translations.ylt: and the Pharisees, having heard that he did silence the Sadducees, were gathered together unto him;
translations.web: But the Pharisees, when they heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, gathered themselves together.

translations.kjv: Then one of them, which was a lawyer, asked him a question, tempting him, and saying,
translations.ylt: and one of them, a lawyer, did question, tempting him, and saying,
translations.web: One of them, a lawyer, asked him a question, testing him.

translations.kjv: Master, which is the great commandment in the law?
translations.ylt: `Teacher, which is the great command in the Law?'
translations.web: “Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the law?”

translations.kjv: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
translations.ylt: And Jesus said to him, `Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thine understanding--
translations.web: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’

translations.kjv: This is the first and great commandment.
translations.ylt: this is a first and great command;
translations.web: This is the first and great commandment.

translations.kjv: And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
translations.ylt: and the second is like to it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself;
translations.web: A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’

translations.kjv: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
translations.ylt: on these--the two commands--all the law and the prophets do hang.'
translations.web: The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments.”

translations.kjv: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them,
translations.ylt: And the Pharisees having been gathered together, Jesus did question them,
translations.web: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question,

translations.kjv: Saying, What think ye of Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, The Son of David.
translations.ylt: saying, `What do ye think concerning the Christ? of whom is he son?' They say to him, `Of David.'
translations.web: saying, “What do you think of the Christ? Whose son is he?” They said to him, “Of David.”

translations.kjv: He saith unto them, How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying,
translations.ylt: He saith to them, `How then doth David in the Spirit call him lord, saying,
translations.web: He said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,

translations.kjv: The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool?
translations.ylt: The Lord said to my lord, Sit at my right hand, till I may make thine enemies thy footstool?
translations.web: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, sit on my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet’?

translations.kjv: If David then call him Lord, how is he his son?
translations.ylt: If then David doth call him lord, how is he his son?'
translations.web: “If then David calls him Lord, how is he his son?”

translations.kjv: And no man was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.
translations.ylt: And no one was able to answer him a word, nor durst any from that day question him any more.
translations.web: No one was able to answer him a word, neither did any man dare ask him any more questions from that day forward.

translations.kjv: Then spake Jesus to the multitude, and to his disciples,
translations.ylt: Then Jesus spake to the multitudes, and to his disciples,
translations.web: Then Jesus spoke to the multitudes and to his disciples,

translations.kjv: Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat:
translations.ylt: saying, `On the seat of Moses sat down the scribes and the Pharisees;
translations.web: saying, “The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.

translations.kjv: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.
translations.ylt: all, then, as much as they may say to you to observe, observe and do, but according to their works do not, for they say, and do not;
translations.web: All things therefore whatever they tell you to observe, observe and do, but don’t do their works; for they say, and don’t do.

translations.kjv: For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.
translations.ylt: for they bind together burdens heavy and grievous to be borne, and lay upon the shoulders of men, but with their finger they will not move them.
translations.web: For they bind heavy burdens that are grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not lift a finger to help them.

translations.kjv: But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments,
translations.ylt: `And all their works they do to be seen by men, and they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the fringes of their garments,
translations.web: But they do all their works to be seen by men. They make their phylacteries broad and enlarge the fringes of their garments,

translations.kjv: And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,
translations.ylt: they love also the chief couches in the supper, and the chief seats in the synagogues,
translations.web: and love the place of honor at feasts, the best seats in the synagogues,

translations.kjv: And greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi.
translations.ylt: and the salutations in the market-places, and to be called by men, Rabbi, Rabbi.
translations.web: the salutations in the marketplaces, and to be called ‘Rabbi, Rabbi’ by men.

translations.kjv: But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren.
translations.ylt: `And ye--ye may not be called Rabbi, for one is your director--the Christ, and all ye are brethren;
translations.web: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi’, for one is your teacher, the Christ, and all of you are brothers.

translations.kjv: And call no man your father upon the earth: for one is your Father, which is in heaven.
translations.ylt: and ye may not call any your father on the earth, for one is your Father, who is in the heavens,
translations.web: Call no man on the earth your father, for one is your Father, he who is in heaven.

translations.kjv: Neither be ye called masters: for one is your Master, even Christ.
translations.ylt: nor may ye be called directors, for one is your director--the Christ.
translations.web: Neither be called masters, for one is your master, the Christ.

translations.kjv: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.
translations.ylt: And the greater of you shall be your ministrant,
translations.web: But he who is greatest among you will be your servant.

translations.kjv: And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.
translations.ylt: and whoever shall exalt himself shall be humbled, and whoever shall humble himself shall be exalted.
translations.web: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

translations.kjv: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.
translations.ylt: `Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye shut up the reign of the heavens before men, for ye do not go in, nor those going in do ye suffer to enter.
translations.web: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows’ houses, and as a pretense you make long prayers. Therefore you will receive greater condemnation.

translations.kjv: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.
translations.ylt: `Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye go round the sea and the dry land to make one proselyte, and whenever it may happen--ye make him a son of gehenna twofold more than yourselves.
translations.web: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna as yourselves.

translations.kjv: Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!
translations.ylt: `Woe to you, blind guides, who are saying, Whoever may swear by the sanctuary, it is nothing, but whoever may swear by the gold of the sanctuary--is debtor!
translations.web: “Woe to you, you blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple, he is obligated.’
